summary: Everyone prepares for judgment in their own language, and Carrie chooses not to interfere when Bjorn puts on armor.

panelPlan.action: Wide. Carrie sorts a thin file into order. Gunnar puts a library book into a bag after being told he cannot read during the hearing. The two male Kin dress carefully in their established clothing with small modern adaptations. Astrid ties or secures her usual outer layer, composed.
Insert. Bjorn lifts his armor from where it has been stored, maintained but not fetishized.
Medium. He puts it on over appropriate clothing. No weapon belt, no axe, no knife.
Carrie sees him from across the room. She starts to speak.
Close on Carrie choosing not to. She instead checks his hands/waist visually for weapons.
Bjorn.

dialogueInline.text: I know the rules of this hall.
Great. That's all I was asking.

directionInline.text: Exactly five displaced applicants are present: Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid and the two established male Kin. Carrie is the caseworker. Bjorn's armor contains no weapons.

summary: Hearing-center security treats Bjorn's armor as an ordinary screening problem, not as a spectacle or threat.

panelPlan.action: Wide. Ordinary metal detector, trays, tired security staff, people removing belts and emptying pockets. Bjorn in armor stands in line with everyone else.
Medium. A security officer looks at the metal detector, then at Bjorn.
Insert. Bjorn places rings and loose metal pieces into a gray tray where required. No weapons appear.
Two-shot.
Officer waves him through after wanding. Bjorn accepts the ruling because it is clear.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECURITY OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: No blades. No loose spikes. Nothing you can take off and swing.

summary: In the waiting area, Astrid quietly demonstrates one small piece of independence before anyone thinks to test her.

panelPlan.action: Wide. Plastic chairs, municipal notices, vending machine, families and individuals waiting for unrelated matters. The household sits together but not rigidly.
Carrie opens the file.
Bjorn.
Astrid notices a posted NO FOOD OR DRINK BEYOND THIS POINT instruction, reads enough of it to understand, and calmly finishes/sets aside her coffee before Carrie mentions it.
Carrie notices Astrid's action, then returns to the file without commenting. Gunnar also notices.

dialogueInline.text: We can run through likely questions once.

summary: The clerk calls the matter and immediately breaks the household's instinct to present itself as one unit.

panelPlan.action: Doorway medium. A clerk calls the matter. Do not letter unresolved male Kin names; the clerk can call the docket/case number and then verify people inside.
Wide. Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid, and both male Kin rise together. Carrie rises with them.
Inside chamber. The clerk gestures to separate chairs / positions for identity verification.
Bjorn starts to remain standing beside the others; Carrie lightly touches the back of his assigned chair rather than physically steering him.
Wide from authority's viewpoint. Five displaced applicants now occupy five distinct seats, with Carrie at caseworker table nearby.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: DTI temporal-residency matter. All applicants, please.

directionInline.text: Seat the five displaced applicants as five distinct people. Carrie remains at the separate caseworker position.

summary: The hearing authority summarizes a competent case file that accidentally makes the household sound more dependent on Carrie than the people sitting in front of it.

panelPlan.action: Insert. Thin but substantial DTI file: housing placement, incident reports, transit/banking milestones, inspection notes, neighborhood contacts, review notice.
Medium on Hearing Officer reading.
Carrie listens; Bjorn looks at the file as if it were speaking about someone else.
Hearing Officer continues.
Close on Carrie. That sentence bothers her because she knows it is no longer true.

dialogueInline.text: Five temporal-displacement applicants. Shared emergency placement converted to provisional residence. Repeated compliance exceptions. No criminal referral. Stable housing. Increasing independent activity.
Caseworker supervision remains the primary documented support.

summary: Carrie's strongest testimony is admitting that successful integration increasingly occurs outside her knowledge.

dialogueInline.text: In your professional judgment, has the placement been successful?
Yes. Housing stabilized. Missed appointments are down. Independent travel is up. Neighborhood incidents are—
It used to be accurate. Now success mostly means I don't know everything they do all day.
